title: Balanced brackets
assumptions: text contains only ()[]{}; dictionary operations and list append/pop are O(1).
rationale: One pass over the text with O(1) stack and dictionary operations per character, so the work is linear in len(text).

title: Palindrome check

rationale: The two pointers move toward each other, so the loop runs at most n/2 iterations with O(1) comparisons each.

title: Subset-sum search
assumptions: values contains positive integers; consider worst-case time over inputs of length n; no memoization.
rationale: Each call branches into take and skip with no memoization, so the recursion tree can have up to 2^n leaves when no early return fires (for example, an unreachable target).

title: Reachable vertices with an adjacency matrix
assumptions: adjacency is a square V by V boolean matrix; queue operations and matrix access are O(1).
rationale: Each reachable vertex is dequeued once, and each dequeue scans a full matrix row of V entries, giving up to V × V checks.

title: Count paths in a square grid
assumptions: blocked is an n by n grid; each cell is processed once and integer addition is O(1).
rationale: The nested loops visit each of the n × n cells once with O(1) work per cell; grid allocation is also O(n^2).
